timeline.body:
Is `get(0)` meant to get top level schema only?
If say sub-level schema changed, and we just `get(0)`, that means we dont treat sub-level schema change as change? Since the snapshot didn't change.
By sub-level I mean some recursive entity in the top level record's field

replies.bodyText:
Extensions schema can only be pdl by design.
Since we are going to remove pdsc support in the future, I feel for new feature, we should support pdl only.

timeline.body: Why do you need separate snapshot directories? Can't we have just one snapshot dir that contains both regular and extension schemas?
timeline.bodyText: Why do you need separate snapshot directories? Can't we have just one snapshot dir that contains both regular and extension schemas?
timeline.bodyHTML: Why do you need separate snapshot directories? Can't we have just one snapshot dir that contains both regular and extension schemas?

replies.bodyText: I feel they are two different use cases. Extension schema snapshot is a default feature, regular one is an optional feature. It could be clearer to keep them into separate directories. Also whether there will be a scenario regular schema and extension schema have the same name coincidently?

```
project.getTasks().named(ASSEMBLE,
    assembleTask -> assembleTask.dependsOn(publishPegasusSchemaSnapshot));
```

timeline.body:
At first glance, it's not obvious to me why this check only applies to the extension task.

Separately, there is a way to describe this behavior more declaratively that you can consider. Your implementation is pretty close to it already.

If you create a [FileTree](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/working_with_files.html#sec:file_trees) that includes only PDL files, it can be passed to tasks that require them through a task property of type `Iterable<File>` (or a subclass, such as `FileTree` itself) and annotated with `@InputFiles`. Furthermore, the property can be annotated with `@SkipWhenEmpty`, which will cause Gradle to skip the task if no input files were found.

The benefit of this approach is that the task will always exist, so a script that runs, for instance, `./gradlew generatePegasusExtensionSchemaSnapshot` won't fail when no PDL files are found.

If you create a FileTree that includes only PDL files, it can be passed to tasks that require them through a task property of type Iterable<File> (or a subclass, such as FileTree itself) and annotated with @InputFiles. Furthermore, the property can be annotated with @SkipWhenEmpty, which will cause Gradle to skip the task if no input files were found.

The benefit of this approach is that the task will always exist, so a script that runs, for instance, ./gradlew generatePegasusExtensionSchemaSnapshot won't fail when no PDL files are found.

I was thinking that extension task will run by default and extension schemas can only be PDL format, so I added this check.  The regular schema task only runs when configuration property is provided.
Updated GeneratePegasusSnapshotTask based on the suggestion.
